def parse_amount(text):
    if text is None:
        raise ValueError('input cannot be None')
    # strip whitespace
    text = text.strip()
    if text == '':
        raise ValueError('empty input')
    # allow leading/trailing spaces already stripped
    # replace comma with dot for decimal
    if ',' in text:
        # only one comma allowed as decimal separator
        # simple approach: replace comma with dot
        text = text.replace(',', '.')
    # now text should contain optional leading sign? reject negative
    # check for '-' sign
    if text.startswith('-'):
        raise ValueError('negative value not allowed')
    # also reject '+'? not mentioned, but zero allowed, positive ok
    # allow optional leading zeros
    try:
        val = float(text)
    except ValueError:
        raise ValueError('cannot parse as number')
    # reject non-finite (inf, nan)
    if not (math.isfinite(val)):
        raise ValueError('non-finite value')
    # reject negative already handled
    # zero is allowed
    return val
